note: Rewritten from Snyder's 1926 description of the new species, the original in English; the species was published as Capritermes (Neocapritermes) longinotus and the description is based on 4 soldiers. Type locality Rio Frio, Colombia. OCR problems: sezment stands for segment; genus names such as capritermes are unstable in the OCR.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head yellow to pale yellowish brown, darker in front and at the sides, with a distinct dark median line from the posterior margin to the coronal suture; sides nearly parallel, but the posterior part wider than the anterior, posterior margin rounded; covered with rather dense long hairs, especially dense in front. Labrum concolorous with the head, long, shallowly trilobed, broad at the apex, narrowed in the middle, the median lobe with long hairs. Postmentum (gula of the original) long and slender, the width at the middle about half the maximum width in front. Mandibles black, twisted, asymmetrical; the left longer than the right. Antennae yellow, 16-segmented, gradually longer and wider towards the apex, longest at the middle; covered with long hairs; segment 3 shorter than segment 2, about as long as segment 4 or slightly shorter; segments 7—12 distinctly longer, then shorter again; apical segment long, slender, nearly elliptical. Pronotum whitish yellow, the anterior margin darker, the anterior part very long and high (saddle-shaped), the anterior margin distinctly roundly concave, hairs dense and long. Legs yellowish, long, slender, covered with long hairs. Abdomen dirty whitish yellow; tergites covered with rather dense long yellow hairs; cerci not elongated. Measurements: soldier total length 7.75—8 mm; head length including mandibles 4.6 mm; head length excluding mandibles (to the anterior margin) 2.4 mm; left mandible length 2.2 mm; pronotal length 0.85 mm; hind tibia length 1.25 mm; head width (anterior) 1.8 mm, (posterior) 1.4 mm; head height at the middle 1.2 mm; pronotal width 1.05 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: A very small species, with a narrow head and a very long pronotum whose anterior margin is distinctly roundly concave; the alate is unknown.
